output.name: Mahuri
output.myth: Orrun the Deep-Whale has been under both seas since before the first net was knotted. He carries the islands on his back, and when he rises to breathe he throws the sea up through his blowhole, and the spray climbs all the way to the Windward and stays there. Hesk counts the drops, as she counts the children who come through winter under Taresk, the Knot-Count Kite. It is why the fish come in. Aun saw the spout once, when his kite was too high and the string ran out, and he hung in it like wet cloth. He shouted up at the whale and asked where the wind stopped. Orrun did not answer. He only blew again, and the spray stood in the cold and did not fall. Skarún, the Hawk Over the Nets, hangs to the west and keeps the gulls off the racks. Tavo, who cannot be bargained with, leaves the spout alone. So when the water rises white beside your boat, do not curse it. Count the drops, say Orrun's name, and tie your knot a little tighter.
output.finding: Find the Hawk Over the Nets in the west of the Windward Reach, then look about one hand-span (20°) east of it, where the Whale's Blow hangs in the cold.
